title: The 50/30/20 idea, explained
description: One popular rule of thumb splits money into needs, wants, and saving — here is how to use it loosely, not rigidly.

body.heading: The basic split
paragraphs: The 50/30/20 idea suggests aiming for about 50% of your after-tax income on needs, 30% on wants, and 20% on saving and extra debt payments. It is a starting sketch, not a law, and many households cannot match it exactly.
Housing costs alone can push needs well above 50% in expensive areas. That does not mean you have failed; it means the sketch needs adapting to your real life.

body.heading: Use it as a mirror
paragraphs: Try calculating your current split and just look at it. If wants are 45% and saving is 2%, the mirror is showing you where a small shift could happen — perhaps moving 3% from wants to saving.
Small shifts matter. Moving a little at a time is more sustainable than a dramatic overhaul you abandon in two weeks.

body.heading: Make your own version
paragraphs: Students might use a simpler version: cover needs, save something — even a tiny amount — then enjoy the rest without guilt. The best budget rule is the one you will actually keep using.

takeaway: Use 50/30/20 as a mirror for your spending, then adapt it to your real life.
